title: Dwyer--Kan equivalences of homotopy Segal spaces preserve diagonal homotopy type
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A simplicial space is a functor $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$; its diagonal has $(\operatorname{diag}X)_n=(X_n)_n$. Call $X$ a homotopy Segal space if each $X_n$ is Kan and, for every $n\geq2$, the consecutive-edge map
$$X_n\longrightarrow X_1\mathbin{\times^h_{X_0}}\cdots\mathbin{\times^h_{X_0}}X_1$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The product on the right has $n$ factors, with target of one edge matched to source of the next; each homotopy pullback of maps $a:U\to Z$ and $b:V\to Z$ of Kan complexes is modeled by $U\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}V$. The displayed consecutive-edge map uses the constant path at each common vertex. For vertices $x,y\in(X_0)_0$ put $M_X(x,y)=\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}((d_1,d_0):X_1\to X_0\times X_0)$. The category $hX$ has these vertices as objects and $\pi_0M_X(x,y)$ as morphisms, with identity induced by $s_0$ and composition induced by the degree-two Segal comparison and $d_1:X_2\to X_1$; the simplicial identities give its associative unital composition. Let $F:X\to Y$ be a map of homotopy Segal spaces. Assume that $M_X(x,y)\to M_Y(Fx,Fy)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every pair $x,y$, and that every object of $hY$ is isomorphic to some $F(x)$. Then $\operatorname{diag}F:\operatorname{diag}X\to\operatorname{diag}Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Reedy fibrancy of $X,Y$ is not required.

The stated levelwise Kan, homotopy-Segal and diagonal formulation is an agent-specified consequence using Reedy replacement and the fact that these localizing maps have weakly equivalent diagonals; it is not a verbatim theorem of the source.
